req.title: Return all players sorted by id
req.statement: The system shall list players in insertion (id) order on GET /players/.
triggers: return all players sorted by id

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-031 requires GET /players/ to return all players sorted by insertion (id) order. Tests must verify: (1) positive — 26 pre-loaded rows returned with HTTP 200 and ids in ascending insertion order; (2) negative — invalid HTTP method yields 4xx; (3) boundary — after inserting a new player it appears last in the list (insertion order preserved at boundary N+1); (4) additional positive — exact count and first/last id values match known fixture data; (5) state-transition — cache HIT vs MISS header reflects correct ordering on repeated calls. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200 not >=200), exact list length (26), exact id values for first and last rows, and strict monotonic ordering of UUIDs as strings compared to the fixture insertion sequence.

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_returns_200_and_26_rows():
    r = client.get('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    assert len(body) == 26
    for item in body:
        assert 'id' in item
        assert 'squadNumber' in item

tests.name: test_get_all_players_new_player_appended_last
actions: POST a new player with squad number 27
Delete the created player to restore state
expected: The newly created player appears at index 26 (last position)
All 26 original players precede the new one in the same order
trace: R-PLAYER-031: insertion order — new record appended at end
BVA + boundary-mutation: N+1 boundary; new item must be at index 26 not 0 or middle
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_new_player_appended_last():
    new_player = {
        'firstName': 'Test', 'lastName': 'Player',
        'squadNumber': 27, 'position': 'Goalkeeper'
    }
    post_r = client.post('/players/', json=new_player)
    assert post_r.status_code == 201
    created_id = post_r.json()['id']
    try:
        r = client.get('/players/')
        assert r.status_code == 200
        body = r.json()
        assert len(body) == 27
        assert body[26]['id'] == created_id
        assert body[26]['squadNumber'] == 27
        assert body[0]['id'] == '97da2849-d73e-4b43-8a90-7d090402c802'
        assert body[25]['id'] == '77a3ac92-52d1-48c4-871c-73988df20dc8'
    finally:
        client.delete('/players/squadnumber/27')

tests.name: test_get_all_players_cache_miss_then_hit_preserves_order
preconditions: Cache may be cold or warm at test start
actions: Send first GET /players/ (may be MISS or HIT)
Assert both responses return identical id ordering
expected: id order is identical between first and second call
Second call X-Cache header is HIT
trace: R-PLAYER-031: ordering must be stable across cache states
STC: MISS→HIT state transition; order must not change between states
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_get_all_players_cache_miss_then_hit_preserves_order():
    r1 = client.get('/players/')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    body1 = r1.json()
    assert len(body1) == 26
    ids1 = [item['id'] for item in body1]

    r2 = client.get('/players/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert len(body2) == 26
    ids2 = [item['id'] for item in body2]

    assert r2.headers.get('X-Cache') == 'HIT'
    assert ids1 == ids2
    assert ids1[0] == '97da2849-d73e-4b43-8a90-7d090402c802'
    assert ids1[25] == '77a3ac92-52d1-48c4-871c-73988df20dc8'
